title: A port or redesign keeps the existing app's behaviour and asks only about a change
why: Your gripe, Oct 27 15:32 CDT (cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh2DRFWTZ5UH6oNvPN87jdc28, with a screenshot): in the Duo "Card in Hand" work for Manifest's phone app, a session marked its plan blocked on what happens to Suspense cards when Card in Hand closes, which the working web app already answers; earlier it invented an "end of mail day" the app does not have.
note: The global rule building-never-guess-answer covers guessing, not asking what the code already says. Fix: a port or redesign brief (designer, builder, planner) states that the existing app's behaviour is the default and each choice cites where it was read (file and symbol); a question goes to you only when the work departs from that behaviour, says so, and is never marked blocking; a question the code or a standing grant answers is refused. Same step (your feedback Oct 27 15:51 CDT, cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh21vJLZeSrqXyLEvzPyoXgLz): the Banchi orchestrator asked you to merge despite standing merge authority, and asked about a "Take all" detail a reviewer held; a session reads standing grants from the repo's CLAUDE.md before asking, and a grant you give in chat lands in the repo (or the merge tool's config), never only in a session hand-off. Check: the waiting-page writer refuses an item on a port with no "departs from" line, and the reply judge flags "blocked on" over such a question. Red first on today's item. Needs no answer. Port: yes, global rules and skills. Placed ahead of c147 (triage, Oct 27): a gripe, and a false block stalls a lane for hours. Doing: lane started Oct 28 01:20 CDT (orchestrator, after batch 2).
